svg.text: Blueprint + build spec · doc CHROMA-BRD-P0 · rev A · DRAFT for review · 2026-10-09
Goal: prove one fader, one flash button and one encoder can drive a real light with no perceptible lag — before any PCB or panel is built.
P0 is a single channel strip: 1 slide pot, 1 FLASH button, 1 ASSIGN button, 1 encoder, 1 backlight pixel.
It is built on a breadboard and a laser-cut test plate that is the same width as the final channel module.
Everything learned here (ADC noise, wifi latency, feel) is frozen into the final spec before ordering PCBs.
STAGE A — fast path, no hub (UDP/DDP)
STAGE B — through the hub (WebSocket → existing hub endpoints)
A isolates input hardware and wifi
from everything else. If A is slow,
B is what the final system uses
for LIFX; its latency decides which
2 WIRING SCHEMATIC (net labels with the same name are connected)
toggled when a packet is sent (t = 0 for latency tests)
STAGE A OUTPUT — WLED node + test bar (bench supply)
LED data pin: set in WLED
UDP realtime ON · wifi sleep OFF
WLED current limit: set to 150 mA for the 7-px bar (≈ 0.1 A/bar in the final system).
Bar must never be mounted against the plate or any wood/paper test piece.
3 CHANNEL TEST PLATE — mechanical blueprint (1 mm = 3 px)
label tape in P0; OLED later
Material: 3 mm matte-black cast acrylic, laser-cut (or 3 mm aluminum on the CNC).
Sanity-check every hole on a cardboard cutout of the real parts first. Datasheet
dimensions for slide pots and arcade buttons vary by manufacturer; do not trust
this table for a part you have not measured.
Plate is the same 32 mm channel width as the final module, so ergonomics carry over.
4 BILL OF MATERIALS (prices are rough; confirm parts before ordering)
Prefer a module without octal PSRAM (that reserves GPIO35–37); USB-C
WLED node; flash WLED from install.wled.me
Mono, B10K taper; buy two if a 60 mm option is wanted for comparison
Cut 7 pixels (≈120 mm) for the test bar
120 mm, mimics the Playbill bar housing
5 V 3 A supply (listed Class 2) + 2 A fuse
Fast-blow, inline holder; USB for each ESP32
Photodiode + 10 kΩ to 3.3 V; phone 240 fps video as fallback
1. Flash WLED on the C3; set LED type SK6812 RGBW, count 7, current limit 150 mA, enable UDP realtime, disable wifi sleep.
2. Wire the bar through the level shifter + 330 Ω; run it from the fused 5 V supply. Verify solid colors from the WLED UI. Check temperature by hand/IR.
3. Breadboard the fader (R1 + C1) on the S3. Print raw + filtered ADC values over serial; confirm T1/T2 before adding anything else.
4. Add FLASH, ASSIGN, encoder with internal pull-ups; verify clean edges on the scope; add 5 ms debounce.
5. Firmware: wifi (power-save OFF) → UDP to WLED. Fader → bar brightness; FLASH → full-white while held; encoder → hue; GPIO15 toggles per packet.
6. Run T3/T4 latency with scope + photodiode. Tune oversampling, EMA and deadband; send rate stays ≤ 60 Hz.
7. Mount fader/button/encoder in the test plate; repeat T1–T4 to confirm mechanics don't add noise (shielding, wire routing).
8. Stage B: send the same events as WebSocket JSON to the hub (stub endpoint or existing /lights/set) → one LIFX bulb. Run T7 and T8.
Hold 60 s; log 12-bit counts after filter
≤ ±2 counts p-p; zero packets while still
Scope: GPIO15 edge vs photodiode on pixel, 100 moves
Same rig; press → full white; release → restore
30 min at 60 Hz traffic; bounce the AP once
IR camera on channel + meter on 5 V line, 1 h at cap
rise ≤ 10 °C; current ≤ cap; cap holds at white
record result (no threshold) — sets fast/slow classes
7 DECISIONS THIS PROTOTYPE LOCKS FOR THE FINAL BUILD
• Fader length: 60 mm vs 100 mm, by feel and by how much panel it eats.
• ADC: internal ADC1 is enough only if T1 passes; otherwise the final board adds MCP3208 (SPI) chips.
• Transport: raw UDP/DDP vs WebSocket for the board, from T3 vs T7.
• Backlight: whether a level shifter is needed on every chain, and brightness cap for the 40-px backlight.
• Bar density: 7 vs ~17 pixels per Playbill bar, judged by eye at 15° aim on real poster paper (cool, low level).
• Go / no-go: if T3 or T4 miss by more than 2×, stop and diagnose before designing PCBs.
Safety: all P0 voltages are ≤ 5 V DC from a listed supply. Keep the test bar away from paper and wood until T6 passes.
